findings.title: TOCTOU race between CountDevices and INSERT allows exceeding device limit
findings.body: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the device count is checked with `CountDevices` and then, if below the limit, an INSERT is performed in a separate database call. Between these two operations, concurrent requests can also pass the count check and insert, causing the actual device count to exceed the configured limit. Under high concurrency (common for anonymous access), the limit becomes a soft guideline rather than a hard cap. Consider using a single atomic query (e.g., INSERT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit) or a database-level constraint.

findings.title: Local cache is set before DB write succeeds, causing inconsistent auth behavior on device limit rejection
findings.body: In `tagDeviceUI`, the local cache entry is set on line 87 (`a.localCache.SetDefault(key, struct{}{})`) before `CreateOrUpdateDevice` is called on line 93. If `CreateOrUpdateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the error propagates and the user is rejected on the first request. However, the cache entry persists for 29 minutes. On the next request from the same device, the cache hit on line 83 causes `tagDeviceUI` to return nil (success), and the user is authenticated. This means the first request is rejected but subsequent requests within the cache window succeed, creating inconsistent and confusing behavior. The cache should only be set after a successful DB write.

findings.title: TagDevice is now synchronous in the authentication hot path, adding latency to every anonymous request
findings.body: Previously `TagDevice` was called in a goroutine with a 2-minute timeout, so it never blocked the authentication response. Now it runs synchronously within `Authenticate`, meaning every anonymous request incurs a database round-trip (and potentially two: one for COUNT and one for INSERT/UPDATE) before the user receives a response. This adds latency to the critical authentication path for all anonymous users, and if the database is slow, it can cause request timeouts or pile-ups.

findings.title: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when device simply doesn't exist, conflating two different failure modes
findings.body: When the device limit is reached and `updateDevice` is called for a device that has never been seen (or was cleaned up), `rowsAffected` is 0 and `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned. This is functionally correct for enforcing the limit, but the error message is misleading for logging and debugging: the device wasn't rejected because an existing device hit a limit—it was rejected because it's a new device and the limit is full. More importantly, if a device was cleaned up by `DeleteDevicesOlderThan` but the client still sends its device ID, the user will be permanently locked out with a confusing error, even though the device no longer occupies a slot. Consider distinguishing 'device not found' from 'limit reached' or documenting this behavior.

findings.title: TypeScript type says `number | undefined` but Go int64 always serializes as a number (0 when unset)
findings.body: The `anonymousDeviceLimit` field is typed as `number | undefined` in the frontend TypeScript interface, but the Go DTO uses `int64` without `omitempty`, which means it will always serialize as `0` in JSON when no limit is configured—never as `null` or absent. Frontend code checking for `undefined` to determine if a limit is active will not work correctly; it should check for `0` instead, or the Go struct should use a pointer type with `omitempty`.

findings.title: No test verifying that an existing device can still be updated when the limit is reached
findings.body: `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only tests that a *new* device is rejected when the limit is reached. There is no test confirming that an *existing* device (one already in the database) can still successfully update its record when the limit is reached. This is the happy path for the `updateDevice` function and is critical to verify—without it, a regression could silently lock out all anonymous users once the limit is hit.
